name: Carrowfield Waxed Canvas Barn Jacket
description:
A heavy waxed canvas barn jacket in faded tobacco brown, cut wide through the shoulders with a corduroy collar and four brass-snap patch pockets. The wax finish has been applied thick enough to bead water without any tech assistance — just old-fashioned textile chemistry. The lining is a coarse plaid flannel, warm but not suffocating, and the whole thing smells faintly of linseed oil and machine grease after a week of wear.

Carrowfield is a mid-tier independent label out of the old Milwaukee corridor, making workwear-adjacent pieces for people who actually work. This jacket is popular with Tier 2 tradespeople, delivery runners, and outer-district shop owners who need something that holds up to weather, tool catches, and the general abuse of a working day. It softens and darkens with age in a way that makes each jacket look unique after six months of use.
what_it_says: You work with your hands and you buy things that last. You're not performing toughness — you've earned it.
story_hooks: A character finds a crumpled note in the breast pocket of a secondhand Carrowfield — an address, a date three weeks past, and a name they recognize from a missing persons report.
The jacket's wax finish, it turns out, is chemically similar enough to a specific industrial solvent that it lets the wearer pass a contamination checkpoint unquestioned.
A Carrowfield factory worker is selling a batch of jackets with a subtle alteration sewn into the lining — something a union organizer asked them to hide.
